question.worked_solution:
The area bounded by a polar curve is given by

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}(\theta )\,\text{d}\theta \,.
$$

When $r(\theta )=3+4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $, ${\theta }_{1}=-\frac{\pi }{3}$ and ${\theta }_{2}=\frac{\pi }{3}$, this gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /3}^{\pi /3}(3+4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /3}^{\pi /3}(9+24\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +16{cos}^{2}⁡\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /3}^{\pi /3}(9+24\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +8(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )))\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(17\theta +24\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )){|}_{-\pi /3}^{\pi /3} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(17\theta \,{|}_{-\pi /3}^{\pi /3}+24\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,{|}_{-\pi /3}^{\pi /3}+4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )\,{|}_{-\pi /3}^{\pi /3}) \\  & =\frac{17}{2}\theta \,{|}_{-\pi /3}^{\pi /3}+12\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,{|}_{-\pi /3}^{\pi /3}+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )\,{|}_{-\pi /3}^{\pi /3} \\  & =\frac{17}{2}(\frac{\pi }{3}+\frac{\pi }{3})+12(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{3}))+2(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\frac{2\pi }{3})) \\  & =\frac{17\pi }{3}+12(\sqrt{3})+2(\sqrt{3}) \\  & =\frac{17\pi }{3}+14\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
